question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

This was not only exciting but rewarding because I was able to experience adventure for the first time in my life.
option_1: This was not only exciting but also rewarding
option_2: This was not only excited but also rewarding
option_4: This was not only exciting but also rewarded
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. This was not only exciting but also rewarding.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correlative conjunction "not only ... but also" must be used as a pair. The original sentence omits "also", so it should be "not only exciting but also rewarding".

◦ Correct: This was not only exciting but also rewarding because I was able to experience adventure ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 wrongly changes "exciting" to "excited"; Option 4 wrongly changes "rewarding" to "rewarded".

• The two joined words must be parallel (exciting / rewarding — both adjectives).

NOTE

• Correlative conjunctions (used in pairs): not only ... but also, either ... or, neither ... nor, both ... and, whether ... or. The elements they join must be grammatically parallel.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and complete the given phrase.

She was on cloud _________ after receiving the scholarship.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. nine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "on cloud nine" means extremely happy or elated. (अत्यधिक प्रसन्न)

◦ Correct: She was on cloud nine after receiving the scholarship.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "on cloud ten/seven/eight" are not standard idioms; only "on cloud nine" carries the meaning of great joy.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of happiness: "over the moon", "on top of the world", "walking on air", "in seventh heaven".

question: Select the option that has used the correct tense.
option_1: He realised he had forgotten his keys after he had leave the house.
option_2: He realised he had forgotten his keys after he had left the house.
option_3: He realised he had forgotten his keys after he has leave the house.
option_4: He realised he had forgotten his keys after he was left the house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. He realised he had forgotten his keys after he had left the house.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the auxiliary "had", the past participle (V3) is required. The past participle of "leave" is "left" (leave – left – left). So "had left the house".

◦ Correct: He realised he had forgotten his keys after he had left the house.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 and 3 wrongly use "leave" (base form) after "had".

• Option 4 "was left" is a wrong passive form.

NOTE

• Past perfect = had + past participle (V3): had left, had gone, had forgotten. It describes the earlier of two past actions.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The Lal Chowk is a large open square surrounded by mansions of the wealthiest classes than educated ones.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. wealthier.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree. The comparative of "wealthy" is "wealthier".

◦ Correct: ... mansions of the wealthier classes than educated ones.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "wealthy" (positive) and Option 4 "the wealthy" lack the comparative sense needed with "than".

• Option 3 "more wealthier" is a double comparative — always incorrect.

NOTE

• Degrees of "wealthy": wealthy – wealthier (with "than") – wealthiest (with "the"). Never combine "more" with "-er".

question:
Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank.

Macbeth believed the witches' _________ about his future.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. prophecy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Prophecy" (a noun) means a prediction of what will happen in the future. (भविष्यवाणी)

◦ Correct: Macbeth believed the witches' prophecy about his future.

• Spelling key: PRO + PHE + CY.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspelt: "tyrany" → tyranny, "questionaire" → questionnaire, "suprise" → surprise.

NOTE

• Note: prophecy (noun — a prediction) vs prophesy (verb — to predict). "The witch made a prophecy" / "She prophesied doom".

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

She often goes / for a walk / with her dog / in the night.
option_3: She often goes for a walk
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. in the night.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct expression is "at night", not "in the night". So the segment should be "at night".

◦ Correct: She often goes for a walk with her dog at night.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "She often goes for a walk", "for a walk" and "with her dog" are all correct.

NOTE

• Prepositions of time: we say "at night" but "in the morning / afternoon / evening". "In the night" is generally incorrect in standard usage.

question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct.

She is the most active and the more energetic social worker in our team.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the most.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To keep the sentence parallel with "the most active", the second adjective must also be in the superlative — "the most energetic". "the more" (comparative) breaks the parallelism.

◦ Correct: She is the most active and the most energetic social worker in our team.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "in our team" implies a comparison among the whole group, requiring the superlative "the most", not the comparative "the more".

NOTE

• When two adjectives describe the same noun and are joined by "and", keep them in the same degree: "the most active and the most energetic".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

We rely on Hiren because he is most intelligent than many other boys in our school quiz team.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. more intelligent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree. As "intelligent" is a long adjective, its comparative is "more intelligent".

◦ Correct: ... he is more intelligent than many other boys in our school quiz team.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "most intelligent" is a superlative and cannot be used with "than".

• Options 1 "less intelligent" and 2 "least intelligent" change the intended meaning.

NOTE

• Long adjectives form the comparative with "more ... than" (more intelligent than) and the superlative with "the most".

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the highlighted text in the given sentence.

The company was rapidly deteriorating when the chairman and some top officials were accused of fraud.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. hell in a handbasket.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "(going to) hell in a handbasket" means deteriorating rapidly; heading towards ruin/disaster. It fits "the company was rapidly deteriorating". (तेज़ी से बर्बाद होना)

◦ Example: With losses mounting, the business was going to hell in a handbasket.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "head over heels" (deeply in love), Option 3 "hitting the sack" (going to bed) and Option 4 "holding your horses" (waiting patiently) do not fit.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of decline: "going downhill", "on its last legs", "falling apart".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

Army officers are given training to decipher the secret messages sent during war time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Decode.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Decipher" means to convert (a coded or unclear message) into normal language; to decode/interpret. Its closest synonym is "decode". (गूढ़लेख को पढ़ना / अर्थ निकालना)

◦ Example: The spy could decipher/decode the enemy's secret signals.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Encode" (to put into code) is the antonym.

• Option 3 "Defy" (to resist) and Option 4 "Decide" (to make up one's mind) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of decipher: decode, interpret, work out, decrypt. Antonyms: encode, encrypt, encipher.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Excessive
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Exorbitant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Excessive" means too much; more than what is normal or necessary. Its closest synonym is "exorbitant" (unreasonably high/excessive, especially of prices). (अत्यधिक)

◦ Example: The shop charged an excessive/exorbitant price for the medicine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Scarce" (in short supply) is an antonym.

• Option 2 "Cute" and Option 3 "Dirty" are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of excessive: exorbitant, extravagant, immoderate, undue, inordinate. Antonyms: moderate, scarce, insufficient.

question:
Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed words correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully.

(My husband and I) are from Varanasi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Both of us.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "My husband and I" refers to two people, so "Both of us" (referring to two) correctly replaces it and takes the plural verb "are".

◦ Correct: Both of us are from Varanasi.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Either of us" (one of the two) and "Each one of us" take a singular verb (is), not "are".

• "Everyone of us" is non-standard.

NOTE

• "Both" = the two together (plural verb); "either/neither/each" = one at a time (singular verb). "Both of us are..." is correct.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. succlucent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Succlucent" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "succulent", meaning juicy, tender and tasty (of food) or a type of water-storing plant. (रसीला)

◦ Example: We enjoyed a succulent mango.

• Spelling key: SUC + CU + LENT.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "subterfuge" (a deceptive trick), "sufficient" (enough) and "sanguinity" (optimism/cheerfulness) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related: succulent (adjective/noun), succulence (noun). Cacti and aloe are examples of succulent plants.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The teacher _________ the students to think critically about the topic.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. advised.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Advised" means recommended/counselled someone to do something. The teacher advised the students to think critically — i.e., counselled them. (सलाह दी)

◦ Correct: The teacher advised the students to think critically about the topic.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "acquiesced" (agreed reluctantly) and Option 4 "assented" (agreed) take "to/in" and do not take a person + to-infinitive like this.

• Option 2 "admonished" (scolded/warned) carries a negative sense that does not fit "to think critically".

NOTE

• "Advise + object + to + verb" (advised the students to think). Note the verb "advise" vs the noun "advice".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Insist
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Urge.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Insist" means to demand or press firmly for something; to urge strongly. Its closest synonym is "urge". (आग्रह करना / ज़ोर देना)

◦ Example: She insisted/urged that we stay for dinner.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Barge" (to move roughly / intrude), Option 3 "Rebut" (to disprove) and Option 4 "Wage" (to carry on, e.g., a war) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of insist: urge, press, demand, maintain, assert. "Insist on" (something) / "insist that" (a clause).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error.

She has taken / nothing from yesterday / and is feeling / nauseatic now.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. nothing from yesterday.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With the present perfect ("has taken") and a starting point in the past ("yesterday"), the correct preposition is "since", not "from". So it should be "nothing since yesterday".

◦ Correct: She has taken nothing since yesterday and is feeling nauseatic now.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "She has taken", "and is feeling" and "nauseatic now" are acceptable in context.

NOTE

• Use "since" with a point of time (since yesterday, since Monday, since 2020) in the present perfect; use "for" with a period (for two days).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Boisterous
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Quiet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Boisterous" means noisy, energetic and rowdy. Its antonym is "quiet", meaning calm and making little noise. (कोलाहलपूर्ण का विलोम — शांत)

◦ Example: The boisterous children became quiet when the teacher entered.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Noisy" is a synonym of boisterous.

• Options 3 "Cheerful" and 4 "Bossy" are unrelated antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of boisterous: noisy, rowdy, unruly, loud. Antonyms: quiet, calm, restrained, subdued.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the highlighted group of words in the given sentence.

There is an increasing number of people who do not believe in the existence of God.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. atheists.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "atheist" is a person who does not believe in the existence of God. (नास्तिक)

◦ Example: An atheist rejects belief in any deity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "seers" (people who foretell the future), Option 2 "cynics" (people who distrust others' motives) and Option 3 "fugitives" (people fleeing/running away) do not fit.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: theist (one who believes in God), agnostic (one who is unsure whether God exists), atheist (one who denies God).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

The strongest suit of documentary theatre lies not only in political insight and ignorance, but also in the variety of aesthetic approaches it makes possible.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Acumen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ignorance" means lack of knowledge or awareness. Its antonym is "acumen", meaning keen insight, sharp judgement and shrewdness (i.e., possessing knowledge/understanding). (अज्ञानता का विलोम — तीक्ष्ण बुद्धि/सूझबूझ)

◦ Example: His business acumen made him very successful.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Perspicuity" means clearness of expression (not the same as knowledge).

• Options 1 "Mistake" and 3 "Discrimination" are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ignorance: unawareness, illiteracy, inexperience. Antonyms: knowledge, awareness, insight, acumen, understanding.

question: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
option_1: The gardner planted colourfull flowers in the gardin.
option_2: The gardner planted colorful flowers in the gardin.
option_3: The gardener planted colourful flowers in the garden.
option_4: The gardner planted colorfull flowers in the garden.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The gardener planted colourful flowers in the garden.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt words are "gardener" (one syllable more than "gardner"), "colourful" (British) and "garden".

◦ Correct: The gardener planted colourful flowers in the garden.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options misspell "gardener" as "gardner", "garden" as "gardin", or "colourful/colorful" as "colourfull/colorfull".

NOTE

• "Colour" (British) / "color" (American); the adjective adds "-ful" (one "l"): colourful / colorful. "Gardener" (a person who gardens) has an "e" before "-er".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As 2023 closes as the warmest year on (1)_________, there is growing global concern about the rise of extreme weather (2)_________ such as floods, droughts and heatwaves. The atmosphere and oceans are warming due to increasing (3)_________ of greenhouse gases, largely caused by burning fossil fuels. This has led to a greater risk of (4)_________ rainfall and flooding. For every 1°C rise in average global temperature, the atmosphere can hold an extra 7% water vapour. When the right atmospheric 'triggers' are in place, this extra water vapour is (5)_________ as intense rainfall.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. record.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "on record" means officially noted/documented. 2023 being "the warmest year on record" means the warmest ever documented. (रिकॉर्ड पर / अभिलेखित)

◦ Correct: As 2023 closes as the warmest year on record ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "absence", Option 3 "blankness" and Option 4 "erasure" do not fit the fixed phrase "the warmest year on record".

NOTE

• "On record" = documented/registered. "The hottest year on record", "for the record", "off the record" are common expressions.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As 2023 closes as the warmest year on (1)_________, there is growing global concern about the rise of extreme weather (2)_________ such as floods, droughts and heatwaves. The atmosphere and oceans are warming due to increasing (3)_________ of greenhouse gases, largely caused by burning fossil fuels. This has led to a greater risk of (4)_________ rainfall and flooding. For every 1°C rise in average global temperature, the atmosphere can hold an extra 7% water vapour. When the right atmospheric 'triggers' are in place, this extra water vapour is (5)_________ as intense rainfall.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. events.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Extreme weather events" (floods, droughts, heatwaves) is the correct and common expression — an "event" is an occurrence/happening. (घटनाएँ)

◦ Correct: ... the rise of extreme weather events such as floods, droughts and heatwaves.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "quietude" (calmness), Option 3 "idleness" and Option 4 "inertness" (inactivity) are the opposite of active weather occurrences.

NOTE

• "Extreme weather events" is a fixed climate-science phrase referring to floods, cyclones, droughts, heatwaves, etc.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As 2023 closes as the warmest year on (1)_________, there is growing global concern about the rise of extreme weather (2)_________ such as floods, droughts and heatwaves. The atmosphere and oceans are warming due to increasing (3)_________ of greenhouse gases, largely caused by burning fossil fuels. This has led to a greater risk of (4)_________ rainfall and flooding. For every 1°C rise in average global temperature, the atmosphere can hold an extra 7% water vapour. When the right atmospheric 'triggers' are in place, this extra water vapour is (5)_________ as intense rainfall.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. emissions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Emissions" means the release of gases (like greenhouse gases) into the atmosphere. Warming is due to increasing emissions of greenhouse gases from burning fossil fuels. (उत्सर्जन)

◦ Correct: ... warming due to increasing emissions of greenhouse gases ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "retentions" (keeping back), Option 2 "collections" and Option 3 "immersions" do not fit the release of gases.

NOTE

• "Greenhouse gas emissions" (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O) cause global warming. Reducing emissions is central to the Paris Agreement and net-zero targets.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As 2023 closes as the warmest year on (1)_________, there is growing global concern about the rise of extreme weather (2)_________ such as floods, droughts and heatwaves. The atmosphere and oceans are warming due to increasing (3)_________ of greenhouse gases, largely caused by burning fossil fuels. This has led to a greater risk of (4)_________ rainfall and flooding. For every 1°C rise in average global temperature, the atmosphere can hold an extra 7% water vapour. When the right atmospheric 'triggers' are in place, this extra water vapour is (5)_________ as intense rainfall.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. extreme.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage discusses severe weather and flooding, so "extreme rainfall" (very heavy, intense rainfall) fits the context of "greater risk ... and flooding". (चरम / अत्यधिक)

◦ Correct: This has led to a greater risk of extreme rainfall and flooding.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "moderate", 2 "gentle" and 4 "average" describe mild rainfall, which would not cause "flooding".

NOTE

• "Extreme" links back to "extreme weather events" earlier in the passage, keeping the theme of severe, intense weather.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As 2023 closes as the warmest year on (1)_________, there is growing global concern about the rise of extreme weather (2)_________ such as floods, droughts and heatwaves. The atmosphere and oceans are warming due to increasing (3)_________ of greenhouse gases, largely caused by burning fossil fuels. This has led to a greater risk of (4)_________ rainfall and flooding. For every 1°C rise in average global temperature, the atmosphere can hold an extra 7% water vapour. When the right atmospheric 'triggers' are in place, this extra water vapour is (5)_________ as intense rainfall.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. released.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Released" means let out / set free. The extra water vapour held in the atmosphere is "released as intense rainfall" when triggers are in place. (मुक्त किया जाता है)

◦ Correct: ... this extra water vapour is released as intense rainfall.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "ensnared" (trapped), Option 3 "detained" (held back) and Option 4 "confiscated" (seized) are the opposite of "letting out".

NOTE

• Water vapour condenses and is "released" as rain. Synonyms of release: discharge, let out, set free. Antonyms: hold, retain, detain.
